Make the recorded ghost-note comparison

Complete Adding a Ghost Note reference

Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped and channel 1 selected. If Oilcan 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable nb_oilcan in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. The numbers 1–64 are step numbers across four bars: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is 17–32, bar 3 is 33–48 and bar 4 is 49–64. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page.

Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.
Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.
Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel.

Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

Add the main hits. Open Pattern Trig on pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 in each bar: bar 1 uses 1, 5, 9, 13; bar 2 uses 17, 21, 25, 29; bar 3 uses 33, 37, 41, 45; bar 4 uses 49, 53, 57, 61. Sixteen trigs are lit.
Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, select Note and set MIDI 36 (C1), select Vel and set 90, select Len and set ½. All sixteen hits now play MIDI 36 at velocity 90.
Select Note. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release. Do the same for steps 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53 and 61, so that the second and fourth beat of each bar play MIDI 37.
Press Play and listen to four bars of main hits only, then press Stop. You hear two timbres alternating on beats 1 to 4 of every bar.

Ghost notes (steps 8 to 10 add the quiet hit to bars 3 and 4).

Return to Pattern Trig and tap step 44 (step 12 of bar 3) and step 60 (step 12 of bar 4).
Open Masks and hold step 44. Select Note and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then select Vel and set 35, then release step 44. Repeat both edits on step 60: first Note 38, then Vel 35.
Press Play. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged. In bars 3 and 4 you hear a quiet third timbre one step before each MIDI 37 accent. Press Stop.

Undo (step 11 returns to the main-only phrase).

Open Masks, hold step 44 or 60 and press K2 to remove the values you set, then remove its trig on Pattern Trig.
Listen
Adding a Ghost Note

Bars 1 and 2 play only the main hits: Oilcan 1 plays MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9 and MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13, all at velocity 90. Bars 3 and 4 add one quiet hit, MIDI 38 at velocity 35, on step 12 of each bar, one step before the MIDI 37 accent. MIDI 38 is a different pad of the Oilcan kit, so the ghost note is both softer and a different drum sound than the main hits. 90 BPM, all notes half a step long. Listen for the soft extra hit that appears in the third bar, about 5 seconds in; it is much quieter than the main hits and the main hits do not change. Build it with the Make the recorded ghost-note comparison recipe.

This is the original recording. Follow the build and listening notes alongside it.

Optional probability variation

Complete Adding a Ghost Note reference

Starting point: Finish the ghost-note comparison above with ghost trigs on steps 44 and 60. This is an optional, player-run probability exercise, not a reconstruction of the recording. At probability 50, each ghost onset may play or be skipped on each pass, so evaluate the range of outcomes over several loops instead of expecting a fixed recording.

Set a dependable main beat. Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability, press K3. With no step held, set the channel default to 100. Check: every main hit remains eligible on every pass.

Check both boundaries. On the full Trig Params grid, hold step 44 at (12,6), set its probability to 0, and release. Hold step 60 at (12,7), set it to 0 the same way. Play: neither ghost note sounds in bars 3 or 4; the main hits continue. Stop. Set both ghost steps to 100 and play again: both ghost notes play on every pass, matching the fixed comparison. Stop.

Try the optional variation. Set steps 44 and 60 to 50 and play several loops. The musical result to listen for is a quiet pickup that appears on some passes and leaves space on others, while the main hits stay present. Which ghost hit appears can differ each loop; no particular pass or captured result is promised.

Restore the fixed comparison by setting both steps to 100, or remove a lock by holding its step and pressing K2. For a captured 0/100 probability example, see Trig Probability, “Turn chance into explicit rests.”

Make the relative-note scale comparison

Complete Changing Harmony with Scale Slots reference

Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped. If Doubledecker or Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its corresponding nb_doubledecker or nb_polyperc mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Part 1 builds the upper phrase on channel 1, part 2 builds the bass on channel 2, part 3 prepares the second key and part 4 performs the change. In the note page, the column is the step and the row is the degree: y=7 is degree 0 (I), y=6 is degree 1 (II) and y=3 is degree 4 (V).

Part 1: upper phrase

Set 90 BPM (Song tasks, Tempo & feel, E3, K3). Leave Rate at /1.
Open the Scale editor (4,8). Slot 1 at (1,3) is the applied slot. Check Root C and Scale Major on the Scale screen; if you change either, press K3 to save it.
Assign Doubledecker to channel 1. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1 and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel. Open Pattern Trig, select pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.
Open Pattern Note (tap Pattern (5,8) until Note is shown) and set the degrees: tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7) for degree 0, and (13,6) for degree 1. Set the channel range to steps 1-16.
Open Masks. Leave Note at X. Set Vel to 80 and Len to ½. Hold step 13 and set Vel to 50, then release. The phrase ends with a softer last note. Checkpoint: press Play and listen. In C major the upper phrase is MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62. Press Stop before building the bass channel.

Part 2: bass

Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and select pattern 2 for the channel. On pattern 2, tap steps 1 and 9 on Pattern Trig, then on Pattern Note tap (1,7) for degree 0 and (9,3) for degree 4. Set the range to steps 1-16 and the channel octave to -1 with (9,8).
Open Masks with channel 2 selected, leave Note at X, set Vel to 60 and Len ½. Checkpoint: press Play. The bass adds MIDI 48 on beat 1 and MIDI 55 on beat 3 under the upper phrase. Press Stop before preparing slot 2.

Part 3: prepare the second key

While stopped, open the Scale editor. Hold K1 and press slot 2 at (2,3) to select it for editing without applying it. On the Scale screen set Root to D and Scale to Major with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save the slot. Slot 1 stays applied, so playback is still C major.

Part 4: perform the change (choose one)

9a. Stopped: play two bars in C major and stop. Short-press slot 2 at (2,3) to apply D major and play two more bars.

9b. Live: while playing, short-press slot 2 at (2,3) at the end of bar 2.

Result check: in D major the upper phrase becomes MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64 and the bass becomes MIDI 50 and 57: the same rhythm moved up a whole tone. Short-press slot 1 at (1,3) to restore C major.

Listen
Changing Harmony with Scale Slots

The same relative-note patterns play under C major (scale slot 1) for bars 1 and 2 and D major (scale slot 2) for bars 3 and 4, at 90 BPM. Doubledecker on channel 1 plays degrees 0, 0, 0 and 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, with the last note softer (velocity 50): MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62 in C and 62, 62, 62, 64 in D. Polyperc 1 on channel 2 plays degrees 0 and 4 at octave minus 1 on steps 1 and 9: MIDI 48 and 55 in C and 50 and 57 in D. Note masks stay X, and rhythm and velocity do not change. Listen for the whole texture stepping up a whole tone at bar 3. Build it with the Make the relative-note scale comparison recipe.

This is the original recording. Follow the build and listening notes alongside it.

CH 2 / Polyperc 1

Percussion Channel

Complete Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example reference

Starting point: the three settings under Before you start are done (90 BPM, steps 1-64, Snap note masks to scale Off) and channel 1 is empty. The steps below build a six-hit drum bar and repeat it in all four bars.

Select channel 1 (1,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Oilcan 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1 to channel 1.
Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 to MIDI 36 (C1). Turn E2 to Vel and set 38. Turn E2 to Len and set ½ step. Every trig you add now plays MIDI 36 at velocity 38 for half a step. In the default Oilcan kit MIDI 36, 37 and 38 trigger three different drum timbres.
In bar 1 (steps 1-16), hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13. Six trigs light on the grid.
Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 4 and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then release. Do the same for step 12. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release, and do the same for step 13. Steps 1 and 9 keep the default MIDI 36.
Listen: press Play and hear bar 1, then three silent bars because bars 2–4 are still empty. In bar 1, MIDI 36 falls on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and each MIDI 38 hit sounds one step before a MIDI 37 hit. Press Stop.
Repeat steps 3 and 4 in each of the other three bars, using the full grid: steps 17–32 are row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Masks and Pattern Trig do not page. Each pair below is a step number and its MIDI note:

Bar 2: 17/36, 20/38, 21/37, 25/36, 28/38, 29/37. Bar 3: 33/36, 36/38, 37/37, 41/36, 44/38, 45/37. Bar 4: 49/36, 52/38, 53/37, 57/36, 60/38, 61/37.

The channel now has 24 trigs in a repeating one-bar (four-beat) drum figure. Press Play and listen before you continue: the same bar repeats four times. Press Stop.

Listen
Rhythm, bass and a changing chord

Oilcan 1, Polyperc 1 and Doubledecker play on channels 1, 2 and 3 for four bars at 90 BPM; a bar lasts about 2.7 seconds. Drums at velocity 38 hit steps 1/36, 4/38, 5/37, 9/36, 12/38 and 13/37 of every bar. The bass at velocity 42 plays MIDI 48 on steps 1, 5 and 13 and MIDI 55 on step 9. The chords (velocity 26, three steps long, Chd1 3rd, Chd2 5th) have roots MIDI 60 on step 1 and 62 on step 9 in bars 1 to 3, and MIDI 67 on step 49 and 60 on step 57 in bar 4. Listen for the chord changing at the start of bar 4, about 8 seconds in, over drums and bass that stay exactly the same. The drums are the loudest layer and the bass is the quietest. Build it with the three Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord recipes.

results.text:
Build the recording: Average, then Higher

Complete Note Merge Modes reference

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, C major and playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable nb_polyperc in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, give it range 1–16 and assign patterns 1 and 2. Turn Lock merged to pent. Off.

Prepare the two-slot comparison with slot 1 selected. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose a task; K3 opens it. In Pattern Trig and Pattern Note, choose patterns from row 1 and edit their steps. On Masks, E2 selects a value row and E3 changes it; hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig. Open Song (6,8), leave slot 1 selected, and set its length to 32 with the length fader at (4,7). Keep slot 1 selected while preparing both patterns and setting Average. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 only after that setup, as described in step 5. Set Song tempo to 90 in Song tasks → Tempo & feel; set channel Rate to /1 on Clock and apply with K3.

Purpose: compare the same two source patterns under two note-merge rules. Average combines overlapping notes by their mean; Higher adds the range between their highest and lowest values to that mean. Notes from only one pattern should stay the same in both slots.

In Pattern Trig, pattern 1, tap steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13. In Pattern Note, set degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 at those steps.
In Pattern Trig, pattern 2, tap steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. In Pattern Note, set degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5. On the Note grid, row 7 is degree 0 and each row above is one degree higher.
On channel 1 Masks, leave Note and Trig at X so the patterns supply pitches and trigs. Set Vel to 80 and Len to half a step. These are the recorded channel masks.
Open Channel tasks → Merge modes. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads ALL. Select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads AVERAGE. Set Song slot 1 length to 32.
Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Keep its length at 32; on Merge modes choose Note mode and set it to UP (Higher). Select slot 1 at (1,1) to return to Average, then play the slots in order. Stop playback when you have heard the comparison.

Listen for: The trig pattern and notes from a single contributing pattern stay the same in both slots. Only notes where the patterns overlap change.

Restore: Select slot 1 for Average. Keep Lock merged to pent. Off and Trig Merge All for this recording, then return to the separate course project.

Listen
Average, then Higher

Polyperc 1 on channel 1 plays one melody at 90 BPM, velocity 80, built from two patterns assigned to the same channel with trig merge All and the pentatonic lock off, in C major. Pattern 1 has degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 on steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13; pattern 2 has degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5 on steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. Steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 are in both patterns, so the note merge mode decides them. Bars 1 and 2 use Average and play MIDI 62, 69, 64 and 64 there; bars 3 and 4 use Higher and play MIDI 65, 72, 69 and 71. Steps 3, 7, 11 and 15 belong to one pattern each and sound the same in both halves: MIDI 64, 64, 65 and 69. Listen for the shared steps jumping higher at bar 3, about 5.3 seconds in, while the in-between notes stay put.

This is the original recording. Follow the build and listening notes alongside it.

Comparing the Loop Alignment

Complete Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops reference

Starting point: the numbered setup in Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops is complete and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.
Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. This same pitch pair also occurs at step 9, so it is not unique. Count phrase starts: after step 1, the two loops next realign at step 13. On step 4, channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.
Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.
Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.

results.text:
Build the recording: Small hours · four bars in C major

Complete Masks reference

Starting point: Use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. If either player is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its nb_polyperc or nb_doubledecker mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Set both channel ranges and Song slot 1 to 64 steps; set Song tempo to 90 and apply Rate /1 on both channels with K3. Check: Song slot 1 shows 64 steps and playback is stopped. Before editing, open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1; select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap (2,2) to assign Pattern 2.

Controls and step map: Open Channel (3,8), select a channel on row 1, use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose Device, Masks or Clock; K3 opens the task. On Masks, E2 chooses Note, Vel, Len, Chd1 or Chd2 and E3 changes the value. Hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to edit its value. Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Step 33 is (1,6) and step 61 is (13,7). These screens do not page; Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Open Song (6,8): slots 1–3 are on row 1; the length fader at (7,7) sets 64 steps.

Checkpoint 1 — bass. On channel 1 set default Note MIDI 48, Vel 70 and Len ½. Add trigs at steps 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57 and 61. Set steps 9, 25, 41 and 57 to MIDI 43; the other bass trigs stay at MIDI 48. Check the Masks readout at one normal step (48) and one low step (43); the bass line now spans all four bars.

Checkpoint 2 — chord layer. On channel 2 set default Note MIDI 60, Vel 45 and Len 3 steps. Set Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th. Add trigs at steps 1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41, 49 and 57; each chord root stays MIDI 60. Check that the chord tones are the scale third and fifth above each root.

Checkpoint 3 — hear the layer change. Press Play for four bars. Hold K1 and tap channel 2 selector (2,1) to mute the chords; check that the bass remains. Tap (2,1) again with K1 held to restore the chords; check that the same four-bar bass continues under them. Stop playback.

Restore: Leave channel 2 unmuted and playback stopped. Keep this four-bar extension in its separate project; the course Masks phrases use different notes.

Listen
Small hours · four bars in C major

Four bars in C major at 90 BPM. Channel 1 uses Polyperc for bass notes. Channel 2 uses Doubledecker with 3rd and 5th chord masks. The channels have separate note positions, velocities and lengths.

Prepare and apply a second scale

Complete Scale Editor reference

Starting point: channel 1 has Pattern 1 assigned and plays a four-step melody in C major with Pattern Note degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3; its channel Note mask is X. It sounds MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 (C, D, E, F). To build it, follow Dig Deeper: assign Pattern 1 to channel 1, add trigs on steps 1–4, set Pattern Note to degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3 in order, leave the channel Note mask at X, and apply C major in scale slot 1. The captured examples below start from the same setup: Save D major, then apply it follows steps 1 to 5, and Prepare a scale before applying it adds browsing a slot with a long press, editing the applied slot and turning the global scale Off.

Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. Slot 1, the left button on row 3, is bright.
Hold K1, press slot 2 at (2, 3), then release both. The title row names slot 2 and a dim indicator marks it. Playback is still in C major.
Prepare slot 2: turn E2 to Root and turn E3 two clicks to D. Release all grid keys and press K3 to save the draft. Checkpoint: tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop. The melody still plays C, D, E, F because slot 1 remains applied.
Apply the draft: short-press slot 2 at (2, 3). It becomes the bright applied slot. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody plays D, E, F sharp, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67). The rhythm has not changed.
Restore the comparison: short-press slot 1 at (1, 3), tap Play and listen. C, D, E, F are restored.

Complete Song Editor reference

Starting point: slot 1 holds a four-step motif on channel 1 (C, D, E, F; MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). To build it, assign Pattern 1 to channel 1, add trigs on steps 1–4, set Pattern Note to degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3 in C major, and leave the channel Note mask at X; see Dig Deeper for the Pattern Editor reference. Playback is stopped and Song mode is On (the default; Song Playback shows it as AUTO). Slots 2 and 3 are empty and dim at (2,1) and (3,1).

Press Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is bright because it is selected. A slot plays 64 steps by default, about eleven seconds at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so shorten the audition first: tap (2,7) to set the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times to make it 4 steps. The length belongs to the slot, so the copy in step 2 keeps it.
Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both. Slot 2 turns mid-bright: it is a full copy of slot 1.
Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.
Press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher. Slot 1 is unchanged. Change a rhythm or a mask instead of the octave if you prefer.
Press Song (6,8) and look at slot 3 at (3,1). It stays dim because it is empty, and an empty slot ends the group after slot 2.
Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 plays the motif (60, 62, 64, 65), then slot 2 plays it an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77), then playback returns to slot 1 and repeats.

Each slot plays for its global length times its Repeats, so with the length left at 64 a slot lasts about eleven seconds. results.text:
Build the recording: Intro, verse and outro

Complete Interacting with Slots reference

Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major, with playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 or Doubledecker is missing from the Device picker, install and enable the corresponding nb_polyperc or nb_doubledecker mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. Give each channel range 1–16.

Controls and map. Press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Trig params. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects the sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is its position within that group (step 33 is (1,6), step 61 is (13,7)). Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range, then release. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. On the length fader, (3,7) gives 13 steps and three taps at (8,7) give 16; (4,7) gives 32 and (7,7) gives 64. In Song Tempo and feel (E1 tasks, E2 task, K3), set Tempo to 90 and press K3. Set each channel Rate /1 on its Clock page and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock. Stop before copying or editing an independent comparison.

Prepare the two patterns. On channel 1, create pattern 1 with trigs 1, 5, 9 and 13; set their degrees to 0, 0, 4 and 0. Set channel 1 octave to -1, velocity to 70 and length to half a step. On channel 2, create pattern 2 with trigs 3, 7, 11 and 15; set their degrees to 4, 2, 4 and 6. Set channel 2 octave to 0, velocity to 60 and length to half a step. Checkpoint: in C major the bass is MIDI 48, 48, 55, 48 and the lead is MIDI 67, 64, 67, 71. Assign the patterns. Before arranging, press Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot 1 at (1,2). Select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2).

Slot 1 — intro. In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16 steps and mute channel 2 with K1 plus its selector (2,1). Check: slot 1 is one bar of bass with the lead muted.

Slot 2 — verse. Copy slot 1 to slot 2, set slot 2 length to 32 steps and toggle channel 2 back on. Check: the two-bar verse has both parts; bass remains 48, 48, 55, 48 and lead remains 67, 64, 67, 71.

Slot 3 — outro. Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16 steps. Set channel 2 octave to +1 and channel 1 Velocity to 40. Check: the one-bar outro keeps the same four bass pitches at lower velocity and raises the lead to MIDI 79, 76, 79, 83.

Play the three slots in order, then Stop and select slot 1. The arrangement is intro (bass only), verse (bass and lead), outro (higher lead and softer bass). This is a separate arrangement example; return to the continuing course project when finished.

Listen
Intro, verse and outro

Polyperc 1 on channel 1 and Doubledecker on channel 2 play a four-bar song at 90 BPM from three song slots of 16, 32 and 16 steps, in C major. The bass plays degrees 0, 0, 4 and 0 at octave minus 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, MIDI 48, 48, 55 and 48. The lead plays degrees 4, 2, 4 and 6 on steps 3, 7, 11 and 15 at velocity 60, MIDI 67, 64, 67 and 71. In the one-bar intro the lead channel is muted and the bass plays alone at velocity 70. In the two-bar verse the lead is unmuted. In the final bar the lead moves up an octave, MIDI 79, 76, 79 and 83, and the bass velocity mask drops to 40. Listen for the lead entering after the first bar, about 2.7 seconds in, and for the last bar, about 8 seconds in, sounding higher on top and softer underneath.

This is the original recording. Follow the build and listening notes alongside it.

headings: Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes
results.text:
Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes

Complete Locks reference

Comparison purpose: keep the note pattern fixed while only the Decay envelope changes. This recipe has two exercises: compare longer and shorter Decay tails with relative turns, then try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. Use a separate project so neither changes your course arrangement.

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and playback stopped. Make sure n.b. PolyPerc is installed and enabled using Sound Sources with n.b.; assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 with range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½. Add trig masks on odd steps by holding K1, tapping each odd step and releasing K1. Select Note with E2; for each odd step, hold it and turn E3 to set the absolute MIDI note: step 1=48, 3=55, 5=52, 7=55, 9=48, 11=55, 13=53 and 15=55. Press Channel at (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap Pattern 1 in the second-from-top grid row to assign it before playing; an empty project has no pattern assigned by default.

Controls and step map: press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1, then turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 to highlight Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open it. On Device use E2 for the row, E3 for the named sound and K3 to apply. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2; E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception, then release it. To add a trig mask, hold K1, tap that step and release K1. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7. Column is the position within that group. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination and release; then tap the destination to edit it. Set Song Tempo to 90 and each channel Rate to /1, applying changes with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock. K2 clears a held-step lock.

Relative-turn comparison — compare longer and shorter Decay tails while keeping the note pattern fixed. In Song, select slot 1 and set its length to 32 steps with no parameter locks; this is the two-bar straight reference. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep slot 2 at 32 steps. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 clockwise by 200 detents; release it. Repeat the 200-detent turn on step 9 and release. Then hold step 5 and turn E3 clockwise by 40 detents; release it. Repeat the 40-detent turn on step 13 and release. Check: steps 1 and 9 form the longer-tail group; steps 5 and 13 form the shorter-tail group, while the note pattern stays fixed. These turns are relative to the current setting; the absolute Decay value shown depends on its starting value and your device. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the plain line.

Separate endpoint practice — try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. In Song set slot 1 to 32 steps with no parameter locks. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set its length to 32. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 anticlockwise until the displayed Decay reaches its 0.1 s minimum, then clockwise to the displayed 3.2 s maximum; release the step. Repeat the 3.2 s setting on step 9. Set Decay to 0.1 s on steps 5 and 13, releasing each step afterward. Check the Trig params readout for the long settings on 1 and 9 and short settings on 5 and 13. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1. On your instrument, compare the tails while the notes stay in the same order.

Restore: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.

Listen
Parameter locks on and off

Polyperc 1 on channel 1 plays an eighth-note line for four bars at 90 BPM, MIDI 48, 55, 52, 55, 48, 55, 53 and 55 on the odd steps of every bar at velocity 70, short notes half a step long. In bars 1 and 2 nothing is locked. In bars 3 and 4 the Decay parameter is locked on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of each bar, so those four notes ring with a different decay from the notes between them while the notes themselves stay exactly the same. Listen for the plucks on the beat lengthening against the plain ones after them from bar 3, about 5.3 seconds in, and for the line sounding even again at the end of the cycle.

results.text:
Compare random notes with and without the filter

Complete Lock Random to Pentatonic reference

Lock random to pent. is On by default. This recipe lets you hear what it does by switching it Off and On with Random Note at 4. Random Note chooses its offsets at random, so listen to several loops: a short run may not include every note.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major; no Trig params slot is assigned yet.

Assign Random Note. Select channel 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to Random Note, press K3 to assign it to the first slot and press K2 to return. The slot reads 0 and the pattern still plays C, D, E, F.
Set the amount. With the Random Note slot selected (E2), turn E3 four detents right to 4. Each note is now offset by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees at random. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note.
Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Close the menu, tap Play and listen to several loops: F and B may join the random notes, but neither is guaranteed to appear in a short run. Tap Play to stop.
Turn Lock random to pent. On and play several loops again. The random notes now stay on C, D, E, G and A. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note, so a plain F in the pattern can still sound. The random stream is not reset between the two runs, so the two runs will not start with the same notes; compare which notes occur, not the order.

MOSAIC / LEARN
Lock lead time

Set the lead time for MIDI parameter locks before their step.

Example
Try this feature
Send lock values before their notes
← Creating a Custom Device Configuration
Selecting an n.b. Player →
Captured examples
Controls

Some synths smooth incoming CC values. A filter or level change sent at the same moment as a note then arrives late and glides through the start of the note. Lock lead time sends each step's lock values slightly before the step so they have settled when the note sounds. The notes themselves keep their timing.

Tap K1 briefly and open the norns PARAMS menu.
Open MOSAIC and select Lock lead time (ms) in the Parameter locks section.
Turn E3 to set the required lead time. The menu displays the selected value.
Return to Mosaic to compare playback.

Worked values at 130 BPM, where one clock pulse lasts about 4.8 ms. A lead of 0 sends each lock value with its note. A lead of 25 sends it about 28.8 ms ahead (6 pulses). A lead of 50 sends it about 52.9 ms ahead (11 pulses). Listen for the filter or parameter change landing before the note starts instead of sweeping through its attack. This global setting accepts 0–50 ms and defaults to 25 ms. It gives MIDI CC/NRPN parameter locks time to settle before the note attack, particularly on devices that smooth incoming controllers. Set it to 0 to send each value at its own step, which is the original output timing. The value is saved with Mosaic's project settings.

A step's parameter values leave ahead of the step, in an earlier clock pulse. Nothing is delayed to achieve this: note-ons, note-offs, live MIDI-thru, outgoing MIDI Clock, Start, Continue, Stop and song position all keep the timing they have at a lead of 0, and gate lengths are unchanged. N.b. players are unaffected.

Because a value leaves on a clock pulse, the wait it achieves is the setting rounded up to the next whole pulse, so a value never leaves with less lead than was asked for. At 130 bpm a pulse is about 4.8 ms, so a 25 ms setting delivers about 28.8 ms; at 200 bpm it delivers 25 ms exactly. The figure follows the tempo, and every value of a step leaves on the same pulse, so what you hear stays consistent between events rather than fixed to the number in the menu.

No step is looked ahead musically: probability, conditions, fills, random notes, strum, arps and micro-timing still make their decisions at their own times. Only the parameter values a step will send are resolved early.

Every note sounds with its own step's values. When two notes on the same MIDI channel are less than twice the lead apart (a fast tempo, a fast channel clock, or swing and shuffle bringing steps together), a value does not take the whole lead: it waits until halfway between the previous sounding note and its own step. The previous note keeps its value through the first half of the gap, and the new value settles in the second half. A trigless step sounds nothing, so it is not the note a later value waits behind. A strummed chord's later voices are sounding notes, so the next step's values wait behind the last of them.

An address that more than one slot writes, whether two slots of one channel or two channels addressing one device parameter, is not sent early: its values leave at their own step, in the order the step would send them at a lead of 0.

Two cases give no lead at all. The first step after Play resolves its lock on the transport's own first pulse, so there is no earlier pulse for its values to leave in and they leave with the note. A parameter that is mid-slide keeps its slide until the slide's destination step, so that step's lock arrives with the step rather than before it. Nothing is delayed to hide either case.

The lead covers the time a receiver takes for a parameter change to take effect, so every value follows the same rule whether or not its step has a note: trigless locks, assigned values and slide values leave ahead of the step they belong to and take effect as that step is heard.

Editing a lock that has already left changes what the next pass sends, and the edited value is sent again at its own step, so the receiver is corrected rather than left holding the superseded value. Stopping playback or using Panic releases held voices and clears pending parameter-lock output.

Average, then Higher

When both patterns trigger on the same step, Note merge chooses the pitch they produce together. Average uses the midpoint of the two pattern pitches; Higher raises that midpoint using the gap between the inputs. Trig merge All combines the triggers from both patterns. Lock merged to pent. is a separate pitch restriction, kept Off here so the comparison isolates the two Note modes.

Range sets how many steps a channel plays before its loop restarts. Here the 16-step drums and 12-step bass begin together, drift apart, and meet after 48 steps at the start of bar 4.

Slot 1 mutes the lead; slot 2 unmutes it; slot 3 raises the lead octave and lowers bass velocity.

MOSAIC / PATTERN
Rhythm Doctor

Select the fifth pattern algorithm at grid column 16, row 2 to capture, analyse and paint rhythm lanes.

Example
← Adding Trigs
Adding Notes →
Captured examples
Controls

Rhythm Doctor is the fifth pattern-editor algorithm, at grid column 16, row 2. Setup and workflow screens use labelled vertical rows. E2 selects an editable row and E3 changes it. The contextual footer names confirmation actions; painting still uses the grid Paint control. Each project retains one captured bank. Select a lane, preview a 64-step window, then paint it into the selected pattern.

Record and paint a phrase

Use Rhythm Doctor to turn a rhythm you can play into the norns audio input, such as a drum loop, into a Mosaic pattern. Before you start, stop the sequencer, assign a device and a pattern to the channel you will paint into, and have the source ready to play. In the example captured below the source is a steady 120 BPM test loop with one thump on every beat.

Press Pattern (5,8) and select the Rhythm Doctor algorithm at (16,2). The norns shows RHYTHM DR with Record READY, Tempo AUTO, Manual BPM and Input STEREO.
Optional: turn E2 to Tempo and E3 to MANUAL, set Manual BPM, and press K3 to confirm. Leave Tempo on AUTO to let Doctor estimate it.
Tap Record at (1,2) and play the audio. The screen shows CAPTURE and MORE AUDIO NEEDED, then ENOUGH / REC OR K3.
Press K3 to finish. The screen shows ANALYSING and the lanes BD, SD and CYM.
When the Window screen reads READY, select a lane: BD at (3,2), SD at (4,2) or CYM at (5,2).
Select the destination pattern on the top row and tap Paint at (16,8). Detected hits flash on the grid as a preview. Tap Paint again to commit; the tooltip reads Pattern painted. Cancel at (14,8) discards the preview.
Press Channel (3,8) and Play (1,8) to hear the painted rhythm.

With the 120 BPM test loop, BD paints a hit on every fourth step.

Recording needs the sequencer stopped, because capture takes over the audio input and analysis replaces the bank underneath whatever is on the screen. So does Alignment, which re-analyses. Record, capture setup and Alignment do nothing while the sequencer runs, and the screen says STOP SEQUENCER when there is no bank to work on instead.

A bank that has already been analysed stays usable while the sequencer plays. Choosing a lane, browsing the recording, changing sensitivity or paint policy, and previewing and painting all read a finished bank and write to a pattern, which is what the rest of the Trigger Editor already lets you do while playing. Starting the sequencer cancels an unfinished capture or analysis and closes a capture-setup or alignment draft, but keeps an armed paint preview, so you can arm Paint, start the sequencer and commit. Rhythm Doctor does not start or stop the sequencer for you.

On an empty bank, press grid column 1, row 2 to begin Record; the press starts the action and its release is consumed. Press Record again to stop, or press K3: either finishes the capture once the screen says ENOUGH / REC OR K3. Until it does, the screen says MORE AUDIO NEEDED, and pressing Record then asks whether to abandon the take instead. Pressing Record on an occupied bank asks whether to clear its capture bank. K2 cancels that question and K3 confirms it; clearing keeps patterns that were already painted. In a ready bank, use E2 to choose Window bar, Window step, selected-lane sensitivity, Paint policy, or Alignment, then use E3 to edit the chosen item. Window bar moves by 16 steps and Window step by one; both view the same bounded timeline. Alignment shows OPEN >: choose it and press K3 (or turn E3) to open its tempo, start-beat, and fine-start settings; K2 cancels and K3 applies the draft.

Before recording, use E2/E3 to open and edit the setup draft for Auto or Manual tempo, manual BPM (40–240), and Stereo/L/R input. Press K3 to confirm the settings for the take, or K2 to discard the draft. Record uses the confirmed settings.

Stereo records left and right separately. L records the left input into both recorded channels; R records the right input into both. Auto estimates tempo and phrase start from the recording. Manual uses the selected integer BPM and starts the phrase at the beginning of recording. Applying an explicit Alignment draft later replaces that capture timing.

To paint a ready lane, select the destination pattern with the top row, press Paint (column 16, row 8) to preview, then press it again to commit. Cancel (column 14, row 8) discards the preview. Toggle is the default paint policy; Add and Replace are selectable on the Rhythm Doctor screen. Painting does not alter the captured bank.

Prime, Cancel and the preview-shift buttons work the same way in every algorithm; see Adding Trigs. In Rhythm Doctor the buttons at (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) browse the recording instead (see Finding the phrase below).

Watch: Pattern editor trig page demo

Set up the analysis server
Prerequisites

Install Git and Python on the computer that will run the server. The Windows steps below were checked on Windows 10/11 with Python 3.10. On Linux or macOS, use an installed Python 3.9 or newer.

Get the Mosaic checkout and enter the server folder:

git clone --branch codex/1.4.0 https://github.com/subvertnormality/mosaic.git
cd mosaic
cd tools/rhythm_doctor_server

Install the server

Windows PowerShell:

py -3.10 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt pyyaml


Linux or macOS:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt pyyaml


Demucs and Beat This fetch and cache their model weights when first used. Let that first model load finish before analysing a capture.

The server provides six lanes without LarsNet: DRUMS, BASS, GUITAR, PIANO, VOCALS and OTHER. To keep six lanes, skip the optional LarsNet commands below and leave LARSNET_ROOT unset. To split the kit into ten lanes, install LarsNet as well. Its checkpoint archive is about 562 MB and is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0; read that licence before using it, especially for commercial work. The following commands fetch the published archive and verify its SHA-256.

Windows PowerShell:

git clone https://github.com/polimi-ispl/larsnet .\larsnet
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install gdown
.\.venv\Scripts\python fetch_models.py --larsnet-root .\larsnet --sha256 dd785d77f66413c5acbd3a4cedac02951578c838496d059930c43f159647c907
$env:LARSNET_ROOT = "$PWD\larsnet"


Linux or macOS:

git clone https://github.com/polimi-ispl/larsnet ./larsnet
.venv/bin/python -m pip install gdown
.venv/bin/python fetch_models.py --larsnet-root ./larsnet --sha256 dd785d77f66413c5acbd3a4cedac02951578c838496d059930c43f159647c907
export LARSNET_ROOT="$PWD/larsnet"

Start and check the server

From tools/rhythm_doctor_server, start it on all network interfaces at port 8420:

Windows PowerShell:

.\.venv\Scripts\python server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8420


Linux or macOS:

.venv/bin/python server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8420


On Windows, allow the firewall prompt on private networks. The startup log should report ready=True. On the computer, open http://127.0.0.1:8420/v1/health in a browser; the response should contain "ready": true and a lane list. Only read the lane count when ready is true: ten lanes means LarsNet loaded, six means it did not. If required Demucs or Beat This models are missing, the server normally exits. The diagnostic option --allow-missing-models keeps it running with ready:false; analysis is unavailable in that state. Keep the terminal and server running while using Rhythm Doctor; press Ctrl+C in that terminal to stop it.

Connect Mosaic on norns

Find the computer’s IPv4 address with ipconfig on Windows, or the network settings on Linux/macOS. If the norns is providing the access point, use the computer address on its 10.42.0.x subnet. Otherwise use the address on the same network as the norns. In PARAMS > MOSAIC > Rhythm Doctor, set Analysis server to the computer’s reachable address, such as http://192.168.1.50:8420, and turn Use analysis server on. Enter the reachable computer address, not 0.0.0.0 or 127.0.0.1.

If the server is enabled and reachable, a successful capture uses its six or ten lanes. Turn Use analysis server off to keep its address saved and use on-device analysis. If the remote request fails, Mosaic falls back only if its local analysis backend is available; otherwise it reports ANALYSIS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE and creates no bank. If you see only BD, SD and CYM, check the switch, address, health response, network and firewall.

Beat This estimates tempo and phrase start from the mix before separation. Treat them as estimates and adjust Alignment when needed.

Install a supported n.b. mod to sequence internal sound sources or devices connected through Crow. Supported mods include:

nb_ansible for Ansible voices.

For nb_polyperc, install it through the Maiden Project Manager, or run ;install https://github.com/dstroud/nb_polyperc in the Maiden REPL. Restart norns with SYSTEM > RESTART so the installed mod is discovered. Then open SYSTEM > MODS, select nb_polyperc with E2 and enable it with E3. Restart norns again; Mosaic can then offer Polyperc 1 in the Device picker. One Polyperc voice is enabled by default. To add voices, open SYSTEM > MODS > NB_POLYPERC from the K1 menu, press K3 to open the mod menu and adjust E3. See the norns mod guide for the install, enable and restart sequence. Adding too many internal sound engines to channels can overload norns.

Example
Try this feature

Context: Add a scale third with Chd1
← Muting Channels
Adding Trig Masks →
Captured examples
Controls
Musical examples

Masks override attributes of the merged pattern data. They can overwrite pattern values or create steps the patterns do not have, and they accept triggers, notes, velocities and chords. Set a channel default to affect every step, or hold a step to set an individual override. Unset attributes use the channel default or merged pattern data. Each Masks recipe below starts from the four-step loop in Make your first loop (channel 1, pattern 1, steps 1-4). A masked value always wins over the pattern for that step; the channel default wins over the pattern for every step without its own mask. The Masks screen shows the value you are editing as you turn E3, with note names for the Note row, so stop on the readout instead of counting detents. One detent moves a note by one MIDI note and other values by one unit.

Masks demo

Before you explore Masks

Open Channel (grid 3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Masks with E2 and press K3. E2 selects Trig, Note, Vel, Len or Chd1–Chd4; E3 changes the selected value. With no step held, E3 changes the channel default. Hold a step while turning E3 to set an exception for that step.

X means unset and inherit, not MIDI note 0. Masks labels MIDI 60 as C3; Fixed Note labels MIDI 60 as C5. Releasing a step returns to the channel-default view. Hold a step and press K2 to clear that step's overrides; with no grid key held, K1+K2 clears step overrides while keeping channel defaults.

04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Try a different ending for a four-note melody

Goal: change only the last note so the same four-step melody can resolve to a different ending; steps 1–3 remain fixed.

Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with channel defaults Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, so it repeats one note four times. The Masks screen shows the note name for the value you are editing, and one detent of E3 moves one MIDI note, so turn E3 until the screen reads the name given below instead of counting. Norns shows MIDI 60 as C3, so 72 is C4, 74 is D4, 76 is E4 and 79 is G4.

Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and, with no step held, the Note row shows the channel default, C3.
Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents), then release the step.
Hold step 2 (2,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (14 detents) and release the step.
Hold step 3 (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads G4 (19 detents) and release the step.
Hold step 4 (4,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads E4 (16 detents) and release the step. After each release the screen goes back to the channel default, C3; each step you set keeps its own note.
Tap Play at (1,8). The loop plays C4, D4, G4, E4 (72, 74, 79, 76). Tap Play again to stop.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads D4 (two detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase now ends C4, D4, G4, D4. Only step 4 changed; steps 1-3 keep their masks. Tap Play to stop.
To end on the root instead, hold step 4 and turn E3 left until the screen reads C4 (two more detents). Release the step and tap Play: the phrase is C4, D4, G4, C4.

All of these notes are in the default C major scale, so scale snapping leaves them unchanged. A note outside the scale is moved onto it. The captured example "Change the ending of a four-note melody" runs steps 1 to 8 on the four-note loop and shows the MIDI strip after each change (its pattern keeps its own velocities, so the recipe's Vel 80 is not repeated there); "Set channel and step note masks" shows the same hold-and-turn gestures on a different loop.

RECIPE 02
Add a ghost note before an accent

Starting point: the four-step loop from Make your first loop, with channel default Vel 80. A ghost note is a very quiet note played just before a louder one; it makes the louder note feel pushed.

Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Turn E2 to Vel. With no step held the screen reads 80, the channel default.
Hold step 3 (grid (3,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 100. Release the step. Step 3 is now the accent.
Hold step 2 (2,4) and turn E3 left until the screen reads 35. Release the step. Step 2 is the ghost note.
Tap Play at (1,8). The velocities are 80, 35, 100, 80: a soft tap on step 2 leads into the loud step 3. Tap Play again to stop.

The captured screen/grid example, Set a ghost note and an accent shows the same 80, 35, 100, 80 MIDI velocities over C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65). It shows the exact mask edits from this recipe. Listen to the separate Oilcan comparison, Adding a Ghost Note: bars 1 and 2 play the main hits; bars 3 and 4 add MIDI 38 at velocity 35 on step 12 before the MIDI 37 accent. This recording uses a different four-bar drum arrangement, not the C, D, E, F loop above. To make the ghost note come and go, continue with Make the ghost note intermittent.

RECIPE 03
Make the ghost note intermittent

Starting point: the ghost-note loop from Add a ghost note before an accent (step 2 at velocity 35, step 3 at 100). Velocity decides how loud a note is; Trig Probability decides whether the trig plays at all. At 50, some loop passes include the ghost note and some omit it; judge over several passes, not from one fixed sequence.

Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. The screen shows all ten slots at once. A slot that has no parameter assigned yet is an empty slot.
Turn E2 to the first empty slot. E2 stops at slot 1 and at slot 10.
Press K2, turn E3 until Trig Probability appears, press K3 to assign it and press K2 to return to slot selection. The slot now carries Trig Probability.
Hold step 2 (grid (2,4)) and turn E3 until the screen reads 50. Release the step. Step 2 now has its own probability of 50; the other steps use the channel default and still play every time.
Tap Play at (1,8) and listen over several passes: the ghost note sounds on about half of them and the other three notes never drop out. Tap Play again to stop.
To remove the exception, hold step 2 on Trig params and press K2. This clears every parameter lock on that step.

Steps 1 to 3 (moving to an empty slot and assigning Trig Probability) are shown screen by screen in the captured example "Turn chance into explicit rests".

RECIPE 04
Add chord voices over a bass

Starting point: keep the four-step loop from Make your first loop on channel 1 and use channel 2 for the chord. The bass device can be monophonic; channel 2 needs a polyphonic device because one step plays several notes together. The audio example "A bass with room above it" below plays the same idea with Polyperc 1 for the bass and Doubledecker for the chords; its notes and levels differ from the values used here.

Set up the bass on channel 1.

Tap (1,1) to select channel 1. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.
With no step held, set Note to C2 (MIDI 48), Vel to 70 and Len to 1/2. Channel 1 now plays bass notes on steps 1-4.

Set up the chord channel.

Tap (2,1) to select channel 2. Open Channel tasks, choose Device and pick a polyphonic voice; press K3 to apply it.
Assign pattern 1 to channel 2: tap pattern slot (1,2).
Set channel 2 to the same four steps: hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 4 (4,4), then release step 1.
On Masks, with no step held, set channel 2's Note to C3 (MIDI 60), Vel to 60 and Len to 1/2. Checkpoint: it now plays single notes over the bass. If the chord channel is silent later, verify it has a polyphonic device assigned.

Add the chord voices.

Turn E2 to Chd1 and, with no step held, turn E3 two detents to 3rd. Every step adds the scale third above its root: 64.
Turn E2 to Chd2 and turn E3 four detents to 5th. Every step adds the scale fifth: 67.
Result check: tap Play at (1,8). Channel 2 plays C3, E3 and G3 (60, 64, 67) together on every step over bass C2 (48). If only C3 sounds, check that Chd1 is 3rd and Chd2 is 5th and that the channel uses a polyphonic device. Tap Play again to stop.

Change the voicing.

Turn E2 to Chd3 and set 6th (five detents): the chord adds A (69). Hold a single step and change a Chd row to give only that step a different voicing.

Chd values are scale intervals above the root, not MIDI note numbers. In another scale the same 3rd and 5th give that scale's intervals. The captured example "Set chord masks" shows each Chd edit and the MIDI notes it produces.

RECIPE 05
Build the recording: Small hours · four bars in C major

Starting point: Use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. If either player is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its nb_polyperc or nb_doubledecker mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Set both channel ranges and Song slot 1 to 64 steps; set Song tempo to 90 and apply Rate /1 on both channels with K3. Check: Song slot 1 shows 64 steps and playback is stopped. Before editing, open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1; select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap (2,2) to assign Pattern 2.

Controls and step map: Open Channel (3,8), select a channel on row 1, use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose Device, Masks or Clock; K3 opens the task. On Masks, E2 chooses Note, Vel, Len, Chd1 or Chd2 and E3 changes the value. Hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to edit its value. Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Step 33 is (1,6) and step 61 is (13,7). These screens do not page; Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Open Song (6,8): slots 1–3 are on row 1; the length fader at (7,7) sets 64 steps.

Checkpoint 1 — bass. On channel 1 set default Note MIDI 48, Vel 70 and Len ½. Add trigs at steps 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57 and 61. Set steps 9, 25, 41 and 57 to MIDI 43; the other bass trigs stay at MIDI 48. Check the Masks readout at one normal step (48) and one low step (43); the bass line now spans all four bars.

Checkpoint 2 — chord layer. On channel 2 set default Note MIDI 60, Vel 45 and Len 3 steps. Set Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th. Add trigs at steps 1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41, 49 and 57; each chord root stays MIDI 60. Check that the chord tones are the scale third and fifth above each root.

Checkpoint 3 — hear the layer change. Press Play for four bars. Hold K1 and tap channel 2 selector (2,1) to mute the chords; check that the bass remains. Tap (2,1) again with K1 held to restore the chords; check that the same four-bar bass continues under them. Stop playback.

Restore: Leave channel 2 unmuted and playback stopped. Keep this four-bar extension in its separate project; the course Masks phrases use different notes.

Controls

Use one shared Strategy selector for channel output. Press grid (14,8) to cycle Skip → Only → All → Foundation → Fragments, wrapping after Fragments. On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 through the same choices; E3 stops at the first and last choice. A successful choice requests immediately, without K3 Apply.

Strategy is the requested choice. Active is what is sounding; Pending is an accepted change waiting for its boundary, or NONE. While stopped, a valid choice applies immediately. During playback, Boundary names NEXT CYCLE or NEXT PATTERN.

Foundation controls trigs only. Note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Fragments controls all four attributes. Retained note, velocity and length settings are labelled inactive and their values read as the saved mode followed by SAVED, for example AVERAGE SAVED. Those rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values while Fragments is active. Select Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings.

Foundation needs a valid assigned anchor. A refused request leaves the cursor at FOUNDATION and shows NEEDS ANCHOR, while Active and Pending keep their accepted values. The next forward detent or grid press reaches Fragments.

Locks

Example

Lock transposition without losing the global setting
Context: Set and clear Note masks at both scopes
Trig Param Locks →
Captured examples
Controls
Musical examples

A lock stores a value on one step, so that step differs from the channel default. Hold the step on the grid, change the value, then release the step. The lock stays in place and the screen returns to the channel default.

Each lock type has its own control:

Parameter lock: on Channel tasks > Trig params, hold a step and turn E3. See Trig Param Locks.
Mask lock: on Channel tasks > Masks, hold a step and turn E3. See Mask Locks.
Octave lock: hold a step and press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12. See Octave Locks.
Scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot on Grid row 3. On a channel page the lock affects that channel. On the Scale page it is global. See Scale Locks.
Transposition lock: on the Scale page, hold a scale-track step and press the transposition fader on Grid row 8. See Transposition Locks.

Parameter, mask and octave locks change their own step only. A transposition lock stays in force on the steps that follow it until a later transposition lock replaces it. A channel scale lock lasts as set by Scales lock until ptn end (see Scale Locks). A global scale lock lasts until another global lock replaces it or the scale track wraps.

To remove a lock, hold its step and press K2 on the screen where you set it. For octave, scale and transposition locks you can also press the same button again.

In this chapter
Trig Param Locks
Give one step its own value for an assigned device parameter, such as filter cutoff.
Mask Locks
Give one step its own note, velocity, length or other mask value. Step locks override the channel default masks.
Scale Locks
Change the scale on a step, for one channel or for every channel. A channel lock overrides the global scale.
Transposition Locks
Transpose the song from a chosen scale-track step. The lock is added to the selected scale's Transpose value.
Octave Locks
Place one step in a different octave from the channel's octave.

Hold the step and press K2 on the screen where the lock was set.	The lock is removed and the step uses the channel default again.
After clearing a transpose lock

After you clear the selected transpose lock, the full phrase plays again while the separate zero lock at step 2 remains.

Open Masks precedence example

The mask-precedence scene belongs to Masks; this lock reference keeps its original placement as context.

Open Masks precedence example
04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance

This Locks note shows how a step-local Note overrides the channel G3 default. Complete canonical walkthrough: Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance.

RECIPE 02
Compare a stored device value with one step-local CC lock

This Locks note compares a step-local CC override with the device’s stored value of 63. Complete canonical walkthrough: Compare a stored device value with one step-local CC lock.

RECIPE 03
Use a channel octave for a bass line and a local octave exception

Start with a routed four-note C–D–E–F phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), pattern 1 on steps 1–4, stopped. Keep the line low but lift its second note.

On Channel, tap octave −2 at (8,8). Play and stop: the line moves down two octaves. The octave buttons (8,8) through (12,8) select −2, −1, 0, +1, +2.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), tap −1 at (9,8) and release. Play and stop: only the second note is one octave higher than its neighbours. A local −1 replaces the channel −2; it is not added to it.
Hold step 2 and press K2, then release. The step inherits −2 again.
Hold step 2 and tap 0 at (10,8), then release. This explicit zero plays the written register on step 2. Clear it with held-step K2 to restore the bass register.

Outcome: an octave exception changes one step, and clearing restores the channel register. Compare the authentic results at Octave Locks.

RECIPE 04
Distinguish an explicit zero transpose lock from inheritance

Start with the four-note C–D–E–F melody. Setup A: on the Scale page, set global transpose to +4. Setup B: hold scale-track step 2, set its transpose lock to 0 with the fader, then release it. The zero lock persists until the next lock or the scale-track wrap. Now compare the lock on step 1 with inheritance.

Hold scale-track step 1 and move its transpose lock to 0 using the fader. The held-step tooltip shows zero: this is a chosen value, not an empty lock.
Release the step. Global +4 remains on the fader, while the step’s zero replaces it when that step is reached.
Hold step 1 and press K2 to clear only that lock, then release. Step 1 follows global +4; the separate zero lock at step 2 remains and restores the written pitch from step 2 onwards.

Outcome: clearing a zero lock restores inheritance; it does not erase the next step’s lock. See Transposition Locks for the direct-tap comparison.

RECIPE 05
Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes

Comparison purpose: keep the note pattern fixed while only the Decay envelope changes. This recipe has two exercises: compare longer and shorter Decay tails with relative turns, then try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. Use a separate project so neither changes your course arrangement.

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and playback stopped. Make sure n.b. PolyPerc is installed and enabled using Sound Sources with n.b.; assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 with range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½. Add trig masks on odd steps by holding K1, tapping each odd step and releasing K1. Select Note with E2; for each odd step, hold it and turn E3 to set the absolute MIDI note: step 1=48, 3=55, 5=52, 7=55, 9=48, 11=55, 13=53 and 15=55. Press Channel at (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap Pattern 1 in the second-from-top grid row to assign it before playing; an empty project has no pattern assigned by default.

Controls and step map: press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1, then turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 to highlight Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open it. On Device use E2 for the row, E3 for the named sound and K3 to apply. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2; E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception, then release it. To add a trig mask, hold K1, tap that step and release K1. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7. Column is the position within that group. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination and release; then tap the destination to edit it. Set Song Tempo to 90 and each channel Rate to /1, applying changes with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock. K2 clears a held-step lock.

Relative-turn comparison — compare longer and shorter Decay tails while keeping the note pattern fixed. In Song, select slot 1 and set its length to 32 steps with no parameter locks; this is the two-bar straight reference. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep slot 2 at 32 steps. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 clockwise by 200 detents; release it. Repeat the 200-detent turn on step 9 and release. Then hold step 5 and turn E3 clockwise by 40 detents; release it. Repeat the 40-detent turn on step 13 and release. Check: steps 1 and 9 form the longer-tail group; steps 5 and 13 form the shorter-tail group, while the note pattern stays fixed. These turns are relative to the current setting; the absolute Decay value shown depends on its starting value and your device. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the plain line.

Separate endpoint practice — try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. In Song set slot 1 to 32 steps with no parameter locks. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set its length to 32. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 anticlockwise until the displayed Decay reaches its 0.1 s minimum, then clockwise to the displayed 3.2 s maximum; release the step. Repeat the 3.2 s setting on step 9. Set Decay to 0.1 s on steps 5 and 13, releasing each step afterward. Check the Trig params readout for the long settings on 1 and 9 and short settings on 5 and 13. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1. On your instrument, compare the tails while the notes stay in the same order.

Restore: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.

Harmony
MOSAIC / MUSICAL
Harmony

Harmony provides Off, Revoice, Pattern and Ensemble modes for channel output pitch placement.

Example
Try this feature
Set the lower register bound to MIDI 50
Harmony: Place two voices smoothly
Enable the Ensemble group on channel 4
← Result and Reason
Performance Management →
Captured examples
Controls
Musical examples

Harmony changes the pitch a channel sends, not its rhythm. Open it from Channel tasks (Voice leading list: Mode, Group, Preset, Tone Map in Pattern mode, Register, Bass, Groups, Rules, Entry, Result). Tone Map is the page that maps written notes to voices. Register sets each voice’s range. Entry holds the Failure fallback. Result shows what was planned and sent.

Captured Harmony range failure and fallback

Captured Harmony Revoice workflow

Harmony offers four mutually exclusive channel modes:

Off follows the ordinary Mosaic pitch path exactly.
Revoice takes the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices after Mosaic's pitch-class decisions, preserving their pitch classes and sounding count while choosing legal octaves and assignments.
Pattern maps explicit effective relative values in the current merge binding to Bass, Inner1–3 or Top. Repeated mapped values reuse one pitch for the entire harmonic frame; unmapped values remain Raw. Random, fixed, absolute-mask and chord-mask events visibly bypass Pattern. Conflicting aliases fail closed.
Ensemble assigns Bass/Inner/Top roles to one to five explicit monophonic channels. Each member retains its own rhythm, velocity, gate, clock and route, but its pitch is replaced by the shared frame. A conflicting local scale lock temporarily uses the ordinary pitch path (LOCAL SCALE BYPASS); a channel or step octave override does the same (LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS).

Register rows set inclusive MIDI Low/High, Centre and Preferred leap for every role. Smooth prioritises literal common tones and economical movement; Compact prioritises register centre/spacing; Independent prioritises movement without a common-tone score. Hard options cover crossing, exact unison, strict leap and strict bass direction. Bass can be Root, an explicit Inversion tone, Smooth or an exact Pedal. Revoice pedals must already be in its input material; only an Ensemble group can explicitly allow a non-chord pedal.

The deterministic solver searches every legal pitch-class placement inside the configured ranges (up to five voices) and never clamps an illegal result. A frame with no solution silences affected mapped voices by default; Legacy fallback is explicit. A bounded search reports BUDGET EXCEEDED rather than emitting a partial answer. Preparing a frame does not change voice history: the first real scheduled onset consumes it, while redraws, rests, failed probability, mute and missing output do not. Delayed strums and arpeggios keep the pitch snapshot made at their onset, and Note Off always releases the pitch and route actually sent.

Captured NO VOICING and Legacy fallback

The Channel grid remains the chronological trig/mask surface. Foundation anchors and additions therefore appear as active steps there. After a step plays, the Pattern Note grid moves that step's bright note LED to the final effective pitch that the native 21-position note range can represent. Switch its upper, centred or lower seven-note bank as usual to inspect octave placement. Raw and bypassed events use the ordinary pre-Harmony position; turning Harmony Off restores the ordinary merged/scale positions immediately. An exact pitch outside that native range has no false in-range LED and remains available in Result/Note Dashboard.

This display is read-only: touching the projected Note fader still edits its selected source-pattern value. Until the changed step plays again, the edited source is displayed rather than a stale output. Final Harmony pitches are also shown on Output (its Pitch and Sent rows) and on Harmony's Result screen, one row per voice as the planned and sent note (C3 > C3). Result uses its Step row to select one coherent event chain; on Note Dashboard, holding a grid step temporarily inspects that step instead of combining it with a later delayed event. A step with no recorded event says NO EVENT and shows no planned or emitted pitch; it never borrows the latest event from another step. This readout occupies the bottom two lines of the Note Dashboard, which is the row tooltips use, so while a harmony event is being shown there the page clears that row and tooltips are not visible on it. Result status names local scale/octave bypasses, explicit Legacy fallback and the specific no-voicing reason. For an Ensemble group, any member bypass or failure is surfaced even when another member has a valid voicing. The projection never writes back into a shared pattern. Copy/save stores versioned configuration, not running solver or phrase history. Missing optional configuration loads as Off; unknown schema versions reject the project before it replaces the active project.

04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Map three relative values

Goal: map selected Pattern notes to fixed Harmony voices and registers, then inspect the planned and sent pitches in Result.

Musical purpose: pin chosen written notes to fixed voices of a chord frame, each limited to its own register, so a note that repeats in the phrase always lands on the same pitch. Choose Pattern when you want to decide which written note goes to which voice; choose Revoice when the chord notes are already written and you want Mosaic to arrange their octaves. In this phrase the notes are all different, so the repeat rule is explained at the end rather than heard.

Terms used below: a written value is the relative note of a step (0 to 3 here); a voice is Bass, Inner 1 to 3 or Top; a register is the range of MIDI notes a voice may use; RAW means the value is not mapped and keeps its own pitch.

Starting point: channel 1 plays one pattern, C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (written values 0, 1, 2, 3; MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), at 90 BPM. Harmony is Off.

Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony with E2 and press K3. The Voice leading list opens with Mode OFF.
Select Mode with E2 and turn E3 twice right (Off, Revoice, Pattern). Mode reads PATTERN and a Tone Map row appears. The change is a draft until K3.
Select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. The Tone Map lists one row for each written value, Tone 0 to Tone 3, all RAW, followed by Reset map.
Select Tone 0 and turn E3 once right. It reads BASS. Press K3; the footer reads APPLIED. Checkpoint: play and stop. C still plays as MIDI 60 because it lies inside the default Bass register (24 to 60), so this mapping alone does not change the sound.
Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right so it reads INNER1. Press K3. Tone 1 (D) stays RAW.
Select Tone 3 and turn E3 five times right so it reads TOP. Press K3.
Turn E1 to return to the Voice leading list. Select Register with E2 and press K3. The Register list opens: Role (the first role is Bass), Low, High, Centre, Preferred leap, Strict leap.
Select High with E2 and turn E3 five times left. High reads 55. Press K3.
Press Play and listen to two loops, then press Stop. The Bass register now ends at 55, so 60 no longer fits and C plays as MIDI 48 (C2), the nearest C inside it. D stays at MIDI 62 because it is RAW. E and F are placed in their Inner 1 and Top registers. Open Result straight away (next step) to see each pitch.
Read the result: turn E1 to return to the Voice leading list, select Result and press K3, then select Step and turn E3 to steps 1, 3 and 4. Each shows its planned and sent pitch.

A repeated mapped value uses one pitch for the whole harmonic frame: if the phrase were C D C F, both Cs would sound as MIDI 48. If a role's range leaves no legal placement for a mapped note, Result shows NO VOICING RANGE and that note is silent. See Captured Harmony range failure and fallback.

Save and Load

Example

← Octave Locks
Captured examples
Controls

Save a named project:

Press K1 to open PARAMS and choose MOSAIC.
Choose Save project.
Enter a descriptive name on the text entry screen and press K3 to confirm. The suggested name is new.

Mosaic writes a project file (.ptn) and a parameter file under that name. Saving under a name that already exists replaces that save. Press K2 in the dialog to cancel; no file changes.

Load a project: open PARAMS > MOSAIC, choose Load, pick the file in the file picker and press K3.

Use named saves for versions that autosave must not overwrite. When playback is stopped, 60 seconds of inactivity normally saves the current project as autosave. Mosaic loads the most recent autosave at startup. Named saves are separate files and autosave does not change them.

Before replacing the current project, Mosaic checks saved song slots, global lengths, channel ranges and scale-track ranges. If a check fails, the screen identifies the problem. The current project and playback are retained.

A rejected load suspends autosave to protect the rejected file. Editing, playing and cancelling a dialog do not resume autosave. A successful valid load, a successful named save or New resumes the normal idle autosave interval. A failed save leaves autosave suspended.

Valid saved one-step ranges are supported. There is no one-step range gesture. Validation covers the saved range structure; it does not check every possible corrupted project field.

Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example
MOSAIC / WORKFLOW
Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example

Build a four-bar loop of drums, bass and a moving chord on three channels at 90 BPM in C major.

Example
← Arranging Song Slots
Adding a Ghost Note →
Captured examples
Controls
Musical examples

Build a four-bar loop on three channels: Oilcan 1 plays drums on channel 1, Polyperc 1 plays a bass line on channel 2 and Doubledecker plays chords on channel 3. The drum and bass phrases repeat unchanged in every bar. Only the chord roots change, in bar 4, so you hear the harmony move while the groove stays put. Play "Rhythm, bass and a changing chord" under Listen to hear the finished result first.

Before you start:

Set 90 BPM in Song tasks → Tempo & feel (E3, then K3). Keep the default Rate /1 on every channel: one step is a sixteenth note, 16 steps are one bar and 64 steps are four bars.
Set the range of channels 1–3 to steps 1–64.
Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, so that MIDI 37 (C#1) in the drum channel is not snapped to C major.

How notes are entered in these recipes: open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). E2 chooses the value (Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4). With no step held, E3 sets the channel default, which every step uses unless it has its own value. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig on it. Hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value. Hold a step and press K2 to remove its own values. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. For example, step 33 is (1,6) and step 61 is (13,7). These screens do not page. Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages.

If Oilcan 1, Polyperc 1 or Doubledecker is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its nb_oilcan, nb_polyperc or nb_doubledecker mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see Norns Sound Sources with n.b.. Build the channels in order: Percussion Channel, Bass Channel, Chord Channel. Press Play after each one to hear the loop grow before you add the next channel.

Finish with a contrasting section: open the Song Editor, copy the song slot and mute one channel in the copy (see Song Composition). Numeric MIDI notes are used throughout, because Masks shows MIDI 36, 48 and 60 as C1, C2 and C3 while other controls label octaves differently. Each n.b. player is unique: Polyperc 1 cannot be assigned to another channel once it is assigned to the bass.
